title: Nullspace-guided Adaptive Bootstrap of Quantum Many-body Systems
abstract: We introduce a nullspace-guided adaptive (NGA) bootstrap method that improves the energy lower bounds of quantum many-body ground states by refining the bootstrap basis in a dynamic and incremental way. At each iteration, the optimized moment matrix reveals a nullspace of saturated positivity directions, which is intuitively interpreted as annihilators of the approximate ground-state subspace. The NGA bootstrap then prunes operators with small nullspace leverage and grows the basis along descendants of these null directions. By applying the NGA bootstrap to the transverse-field Ising chain, we obtain nearly exact energy lower bounds because the algorithm automatically discovers the eigenoperator structure in terms of Jordan-Wigner fermions from a minimal local bootstrap basis. For the Hubbard chain, it improves upon state-of-the-art energy lower bounds by up to two orders of magnitude, reaching errors ranging from $10^{-3}$ down to $10^{-5}$ in the strongly correlated regimes. We further show that the NGA framework can be used to improve the certified two-sided bounds on general observables. In addition, the bootstrap error decreases approximately as a power law with increasing computational resources. These results suggest that our method provides a practical and scalable route toward accurate bootstrap of general quantum many-body systems.
summary: This paper introduces a Nullspace-guided Adaptive Bootstrap (NGA) method to calculate highly accurate lower bounds on the ground-state energy of quantum many-body systems. By iteratively refining the operator basis using the nullspace of the moment matrix, it systematically improves upon existing state-of-the-art bounds for models like the Hubbard chain. This provides a scalable, rigorous theoretical tool for studying strongly correlated quantum matter.
main_problem: The primary challenge is determining the ground-state energy of interacting quantum many-body systems, which is computationally intractable due to the exponential growth of the Hilbert space.
main_result: The proposed Nullspace-guided Adaptive Bootstrap (NGA) method achieves significantly improved energy lower bounds, reaching errors down to $10^{-5}$ for the Hubbard chain, and automatically discovering exact structures for the Ising chain.
method: The method uses an iterative, adaptive bootstrap approach that refines the basis for a Semidefinite Program (SDP) by analyzing and growing along the nullspace of the optimized moment matrix.
model_or_system: The method is applied to model quantum many-body systems, specifically tested on the transverse-field Ising chain and the Hubbard chain, utilizing symmetry constraints (like particle-hole and $\eta$-pairing) to simplify the SDP formulation.
key_observables: Energy lower bound ($E_{	ext{SDP}}$), Moment Matrix ($M$), Nullspace structure, and the error gap relative to the true ground state energy ($E_0$).
important_parameters: Interaction strength ($U$), hopping parameter ($t$), transverse field ($h$), and the system size ($L$).
main_assumptions: The method relies on the assumption that the optimal moment functional admits a normalized PSD realization, and its complexity is limited by the size of the operator basis.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the nesting of variational states and the schematic workflow of the NGA bootstrap, showing the iterative process of solving the SDP, extracting the nullspace, pruning, and growing the basis.
paper_structure: The paper systematically introduces the NGA bootstrap, details the mathematical machinery for enforcing symmetries (Ward identities, PH symmetry, etc.) to simplify the moment matrix constraints, and then applies this machinery to the Ising and Hubbard models to demonstrate convergence.
why_interesting: While focused on strongly correlated systems, the underlying mathematical framework—using nullspace analysis and symmetry constraints to constrain high-dimensional SDPs—is a powerful, generalizable technique relevant to finding ground states in complex quantum models.
